## v0.2.0 — World handling                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Worlds are now identified by their Archipelago binding, and every world must be an Archipelago world.                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  ### ✨What's New                                                                                                                                                                      
  - World-selection list shows **`slot - address:port (last played)`** (green) for Archipelago worlds; non-Archipelago worlds are flagged **"Not compatible with Archipelago"**  
  in red.                                                                                                                                                                        
  - **Multiple worlds** are now supported — the single-world restriction is gone.                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  ### 🔒 Behavior changes                                                                                                                                                        
  - You can no longer **create** a world without an Archipelago slot name.                                                                                                       
  - You can no longer **join** a world that has no Archipelago credentials.                                                                                                      
  - Per-world Archipelago files now live in a **`<world>/archipelago/`** subfolder. Existing worlds keep working (old files are still read and migrate on next save).            
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  ### ⚠️ Note                                                                                                                                                                    
  Vanilla / non-Archipelago worlds are unjoinable while this mod is installed.

v0.3.0.description:
## v0.3.0 — Knowledge gates, per-route item gating, and a tracker that tells the truth

> **A newer release is available: [v0.4.0](https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEM-Archipelago-Minecraft/releases/tag/v0.4.0).** It also corrects a Known Issue below — the "bare region test" list said four checks; there were 107.

Two new option families, a new tracker tier, and a long tail of logic corrections — most of which come down to the same thing: checks that asked for nothing.

### 📦 Downloads

| File | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| `aem-0.3.0+26.1.2.jar` | your Fabric `mods/` folder (Minecraft 26.1.2) |
| `minecraft_aem-0.3.0.apworld` | your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder |
| `minecraft_aem-0.3.0.yaml` | template config — edit and drop in `Players/` |

The mod and the apworld are version-locked to each other; run them as a pair.

### ✨ New options

**`knowledge_gates`** — pick which Knowledge gates a run uses: by category preset (`tool`, `armor`, `misc`, `station`, `container`), by `All`, by individual name, or by negation (`-Chest`). A gate you don't list is off entirely — its item isn't in the pool and the thing it would have held back is free from the start. Station and container gates block *using* a block as well as making it, so a furnace found in a village won't open until its Knowledge arrives.

**`item_gate_behavior`** — per-route control over what a still-locked item does, split into `crafting` / `station` / `container` / `pickup` / `given`. This adds a new `/give` gate. A config written before the split still behaves exactly as it did.

### 🟡 Tracker: a yellow tier

The randomizer deliberately ignores routes it can't count on — a 2% barter, a chest in a structure the seed doesn't treat as progression, a Wandering Trader who has to turn up with the right offer. That keeps seeds honest, but it left the tracker painting genuinely doable checks red.

The apworld now ships a second, permissive graph purely for display. Those checks read **yellow**: possible right now if the game cooperates, never something fill relies on. Item placement is identical either way (`glitch_logic` is display-only).

**Checks re-colour on a check, not just on an item.** A completed location is a fact the reachability pass starts from, so finishing one re-colours everything behind it without waiting for the next item to land.

### 🔧 Logic corrections

A run of checks compiled to a bare region test — "be in the Overworld" — and read green on a fresh world:

| Check | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Withering Heights | `Region(Overworld)` | the Wither is buildable: soul sand + wither skeleton skulls, both Nether |
| Eye Spy | `Region(Overworld)` | a stronghold you can actually locate |
| Good as New | species only | the wolf **and** the armor its predicate demands |
| Smells Interesting | "mine a sniffer egg" | a brush, and a warm ocean ruin to use it in |
| Total Beelocation | "reach a bee" | a Silk Touch tool |
| the entire End tab | `Region(The End)` | see below |

**The End is two places.** The central island is what the portal drops you on. End Cities, elytra, shulkers, the dragon egg, a second dragon — all of that is on the outer islands, reachable only through a gateway, which doesn't exist until the dragon dies. Stepping through the portal used to make the lot of them reachable, *including killing the dragon itself*: kill criteria were gated on reaching the victim rather than on being able to defeat it.

**The eyes go in the portal.** They were attached to finding the stronghold, which is wrong in both directions — you can dig into a stronghold once you know where it is, and no amount of standing in one opens the gate. The Overworld→End edge now asks for the unlock item, a stronghold, and the eyes.

**Structures need finding.** Logic used to assume you'd wander until you tripped over a mansion. The Structure Finder is now the route strict logic counts on, at tier 3 — the copy that reveals half of everything findable, where the first two only show the nearest few by distance. Tiers 1–2 and plain exploring stay in the glitch graph. A stronghold gets no exploring pass at all (nothing on the surface to find) and takes Eyes of Ender as its dependable alternate. With the option off, no such item exists and the requirement vanishes.

**An enchantment requirement read as no requirement** — `_enchant_gate` matched a bare `enchantments` key while the data spells it `minecraft:enchantments`.

### 🐛 Mod fix

**Connecting a slot now forgets the last one.** The registries hang off one process-wide service, so a second slot inherited the first one's locations, checks and items — the advancement tracker was still showing the previous seed. State now resets on the `Connected` packet, and deliberately *not* on disconnect, where it would silently unlock the world mid-game.

### ✅ Verification

`verify_rule_refs`, `verify_reachability`, `verify_all_options` and `logic_selfcheck` all pass, on both start dimensions. Tracker behaviour was exercised in a client against a live server: Finder tiers 0→3 move the tab from 25 green / 36 yellow to 62 green / 0 yellow in one step, with Eye Spy going red→green and `The End?` staying red at every tier.

### ⚠️ Known issues

- **Generation intermittently fails** with `Not all required items reachable: Advancement: Why do I hear boss music? (Bacap)` on multi-slot seeds that include BACAP — roughly one run in two on the configuration where it was measured, against a clean baseline. It is **not** a dead seed and not a logic error: the location is reachable, and the stall is in AP's `create_playthrough` culling stage, which runs *after* fill has already succeeded. Re-running Generate clears it. Cause still open; three attempted fixes were tried and reverted.
- ~~A number of checks still compile to a bare region test — `Sweet Dreams`, `Little Sniffs`, `Planting the Past`, `Who Needs Rockets?` among them. Same class as the table above, not yet done.~~

  **Corrected in [v0.4.0](https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEM-Archipelago-Minecraft/releases/tag/v0.4.0).** That list was from memory and badly understated it: there were **107**, not four. v0.4.0 enumerates them with `tools/audit_bare_rules.py` — a structural test rather than a guess — and fixes 45, including all four named here. 62 remain, mostly "collect an item" checks where the item genuinely is free.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEM-Archipelago-Minecraft/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0

v0.4.0.description:
## v0.4.0 — Every check that asked for nothing

v0.3.0 fixed six advancements whose criteria compiled to nothing meaningful, so their rule was a bare region test — "be in the Overworld" — and the tile read green on a fresh world. Its notes listed four more, remembered rather than counted.

The real number was **107**. This release enumerates them and fixes **45**.

### 📦 Downloads

| File | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| `aem-0.4.0+26.1.2.jar` | your Fabric `mods/` folder (Minecraft 26.1.2) |
| `minecraft_aem-0.4.0.apworld` | your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder |
| `minecraft_aem-0.4.0.yaml` | template config — edit and drop in `Players/` |

The mod and the apworld are version-locked to each other; run them as a pair.

### ⚠️ Behaviour change: `challenge_sanity`

**Read this one if you have an existing YAML.** `challenge_sanity` is now a choice of three rather than on/off:

- **`none`** (default) — no challenge advancements become checks.
- **`frames`** — every challenge-frame advancement becomes a check, *except* BlazeandCave's "Super Challenges" tab.
- **`all`** — the above plus that tab.

`true` still parses, and maps to `frames`; `false` maps to `none`. So an old config keeps working — but **`true` no longer pulls in the challenges tab**, and a seed that used to include those 41 locations will now have 41 fewer. Ask for `all` if you want them back.

The reason for the split: BACAP scatters ordinary challenge tiles across most of its tabs, and the frame alone cannot tell those apart from the challenges tab itself, which is a different order of grind — travel a million blocks, build to the world height in every dimension. Only the tab separates them, so the option now addresses the tab.

### 🔍 The audit

`tools/audit_bare_rules.py` enumerates these checks exactly — no grepping. Every rule node already reports whether any leaf is a real gate, so a rule that demands no item and no other check is detected structurally rather than guessed at. `docs/bare_rule_backlog.md` is the generated checklist and regenerates in place.

Two things make the raw list misleading, and both are handled.

**Gating nothing is usually correct.** `Kelp me!` compiles its criterion into "obtain kelp", and kelp really is free — that rule is right. `Sweet Dreams` reduced to the same shape for the opposite reason: `slept_in_bed` *had* a handler, which returned "be in the Overworld" on the reasoning that a bed needs wool and planks, and then never asked for either. Identical shape, opposite meaning, so each criterion is classified by cause and a human judges.

**A gate only exists if an option put an item behind it**, so a check reads ungated merely because the run has nothing to demand. Auditing with the locks off inflated the list to 267.

Nothing came back as *uncompiled* — the trigger compiler has full coverage. Every one of the 107 was a handler that returned something free.

### 🔧 What was fixed

Nearly every fix is a root cause rather than a per-advancement patch.

**Handlers were ignoring where the criterion says you must be.** `enter_block`, `placed_block` and `ride_entity_in_lava` each dropped the predicate carrying the location. That predicate is usually most of the requirement: Ancient Restoration wants the portal block *inside a ruined portal*, Hot Chocolate is cocoa *in the Nether*, Feels Like Home is riding a strider *in the Overworld* — which means leading one back through a portal, the entire point of the advancement. About 25 checks between them.

**Coordinates were deliberately treated as "not a logic gate".** They are one wherever the game gives you no way to stand there unequipped:

| Where | Now needs |
|---|---|
| `y ≥ 320` | flight — above the build ceiling there is nothing to pillar up on |
| the Nether roof | an ender pearl, up through the gaps (Limbo Walker) |
| *inside* the roof layer | piston + TNT + pearl — you have to open the bedrock (Inception) |
| under the Nether's lava sea | a pickaxe (The Descent) |
| 10,000 blocks out | an elytra (I'm Coming Back, Murph!) |

**Blocks and items with no acquisition record read as free.** A nether portal block is not Nether-only — you stand in one the moment you light a frame in the Overworld — so it costs obsidian, not a dimension. Soul sand and soul fire are not Nether-exclusive either; an Ancient City generates both. Cobweb comes from a mineshaft, village, stronghold or mansion. A filled cauldron is a placed block, never an item: the cauldron plus the bucket that filled it. Chorus grows only on the outer End islands, which are behind a gateway that does not exist until the dragon dies. A grass block comes up whole only with Silk Touch.

**Two mobs had no source at all.** A sniffer never spawns — every one hatched from an egg brushed out of a warm ocean ruin — and a creaking exists only in a Pale Garden.

**The Nether round trip.** On a Nether start, "We Need to Go Deeper" was free from turn one: the check reduced to "be in the Nether", which is where you wake up. The trigger fires on *changing* dimension, so it needs the whole Overworld trip and a walk back.

**Pyromaniac is no longer required to build a portal.** It gates flint and steel and fire charges, but nothing stops you lighting a frame from lava — beside any flammable block in the Overworld, beside netherrack in the Nether — and both portal edges already prove you have lava. Requiring the Knowledge invented a lock the game does not have.

### 🟡 Yellow where you'd expect it

Two new ideas keep strict logic honest without painting doable checks red.

A **waived requirement** is one strict logic buys but a patient player can do without. An elytra is how anyone travels 10,000 blocks and fill places items as if it were required — but you can boat it, so the tile reads yellow rather than red. The Biome Finder works the same way: it is how you are expected to reach a named biome, and wandering there is slow but real.

An **extra route** is the mirror: a trick that exists only for display. An enderman will pick up a grass block and set it down again, which is real but not something item placement should lean on.

### ✅ Verification

`verify_rule_refs`, `verify_reachability`, `verify_all_options` and `logic_selfcheck` all pass on both start dimensions.

`verify_all_options` gained a BACAP pass, and it was overdue: its maximum-restriction sweep never enabled BlazeandCave, so 1,012 BACAP locations — including the whole challenges tab — were never checked for reachability. **1,224 BACAP locations are now verified reachable on both starts**, so none of the new requirements creates a dead check.

### 📋 Still open

**62 checks** still compile to a bare region test, led by "collect an item" checks where the item genuinely is free. That is an expectation rather than a verified fact; the list regenerates with:

```
python tools/audit_bare_rules.py --all --markdown --out docs/bare_rule_backlog.md
```

The intermittent generation failure on `Why do I hear boss music?` from v0.3.0 is unchanged — it is in Archipelago's post-fill culling stage, not our logic, and re-running Generate clears it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEM-Archipelago-Minecraft/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

v0.5.0.description:
# AEMinecraft v0.5.0

The big one: **you can play with friends now**, and your world no longer stops being playable
when Archipelago isn't reachable.

Grab both files below — the mod `.jar` and the `.apworld` — from this same release. They have to
match.

---

## Play with friends

A Minecraft world is one Archipelago slot, and now a whole group can play that slot together, on
LAN or on a dedicated server.

- **Everyone's progress counts as the run's progress.** Advancements are shared — including
  half-finished ones, so your thirty biomes and your friend's ten add up to Adventuring Time.
  A check is sent once, by whoever gets there first.
- **You still get your own rewards.** Everyone completes the shared advancement for real, so
  everyone opens their own BACAP reward chest and gets their own trophy. Filler buffs go to every
  player too, including the ones that arrived while you were logged off.
- **Traps hit the people who are actually there**, and are never banked up to dump on whoever logs
  in next.
- **DeathLink is proportionate.** A death arriving from another world takes one random player, not
  the whole server. Operators can switch it off for the run with `/aem deathlink off`.
- Log in late, or first after a restart, and you're caught up on everything the run has done.

Running a dedicated server takes one config file. Setup guide: **docs/setup_en.md**, "Playing With
Friends".

## Keep playing when Archipelago isn't there

Once your world has connected **once**, it remembers what it needs. After that:

- The room being down — or dropping mid-session — doesn't end your run. You keep playing.
- Everything the world decides for itself keeps working exactly as strictly as before: locks,
  advancements, the tracker, the in-logic indicator.
- Checks you earn while offline are saved in the world and sent the moment you're back. They
  survive restarts and crashes.
- What waits for the link is what genuinely needs it: items other worlds send you, and Archipelago
  chat.

`/aem status` tells you where you stand; `/aem reconnect` gets you back on and flushes what you
earned.

Good for async games, flaky connections, and playing on a plane.

## ⚠️ The game is now called "AEMinecraft"

It used to be `Minecraft [AEM]`. Before you play v0.5.0:

1. **Update the mod jar and the apworld together.** An older jar can't join a v0.5.0 room — it
   still introduces itself by the old name.
2. **Update your YAML**: the `game:` line and the option-block heading both become `AEMinecraft`.
   The `template.yaml` attached to this release is already correct.

Seeds you generated with an older apworld need the older mod, so finish those runs before you
upgrade.

## Fixes you'll notice

- **Traps can hurt you; they can't rob you.** No more losing your inventory or waking up to your
  base rearranged. They also space themselves out and don't all fire at once when you reconnect.
- **The finder bar points at what's near you**, not near world spawn, and comes back after a
  reconnect instead of disappearing for good.
- **Chat behaves.** Messages you type are no longer swallowed as Archipelago commands.
- **The randomizer understands advancements much better.** Requirements that used to read as free
  — enchantments, damage types, mob variants and mounts, where a block is placed, what a container
  holds, brewing, BACAP's potion goals — are now understood properly. In practice: fewer checks
  that look reachable and aren't, and fewer that let you skip past a gate you were meant to open.
- **Spears** are gated by Knowledge: Spear Handling, as they always should have been.
- A **raid** won't start until every raid mob is unlocked, and your Bad Omen is kept rather than
  quietly spent.
- Locked mobs no longer take up the mob cap, so the mobs you *can* meet actually spawn.
- New: **`/aem structures`** lists structures held back by locks, and can recover them.

## Requirements

Minecraft **26.1.2**, Fabric Loader **0.19.2+**, Fabric API, Archipelago **0.6.7+**.
BACAP `1.20.3` is optional.

## Something look wrong?

Multiplayer and offline play are new, and a couple of the lock fixes are freshly baked — if you see
a locked mob riding another, a raid misbehaving, or anything odd after a reconnect, please open an
issue with your YAML and what you were doing.
v0.5.0.title: v0.5.0

v0.5.1.description:
## AEMinecraft v0.5.1

A maintenance release: one generation failure fixed, and a round of corrections to the
logic that decides when a check is reachable.

### Fixed

**Generation failed with BlazeandCave's Advancements Pack and `challenge_sanity: all`.**
Any seed combining those two options crashed during generation and produced no output.
The cause was a loop in the logic for BACAP's "Super Challenges" tab. These seeds now
generate normally. Other `challenge_sanity` settings were never affected.

### Improved

**Sixteen checks no longer come for free.** Each of them could previously be completed
without owning anything the randomizer had placed, which let progression open up earlier
than intended. They now ask for what the game actually requires — among them:

- items that can only be collected with **shears** or **Silk Touch**, such as glow lichen,
  dead bushes, grass, ferns, vines and mushroom blocks
- **nether wart**, which only grows inside Nether Fortresses and Bastion Remnants, and
  previously opened the entire brewing tree on arrival in the Nether
- **wither roses**, which require defeating the Wither
- **string** from cobwebs, and **carved pumpkins**

Tool requirements are now read directly from the game files, so they stay correct as
Minecraft changes.

### Upgrading

- The mod and the apworld are released together and should be used as a matched set.
- Seeds generated with v0.5.0 are unaffected and can be finished as they are.
- Because the logic is stricter, regenerating an existing v0.5.0 seed with v0.5.1 will
  produce a different placement. Generate a new seed rather than expecting the old one to
  be reproduced.
- No YAML changes are required.
v0.5.1.title: v0.5.1
